.github/workflows/chart-repair.yml.content:
name: chart repair
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      chart: {required: true, type: string}
      version: {required: true, type: string}
permissions: {contents: read}
concurrency: {group: "hiroba-release-${{ github.repository }}", cancel-in-progress: false}
jobs:
  resolve:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs: {source-sha: "${{ steps.source.outputs.sha }}"}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with: {path: consumer, fetch-depth: 0}
      - id: source
        env: {CHART: "${{ inputs.chart }}", VERSION: "${{ inputs.version }}"}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [[ "$CHART" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || exit 2
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]] || exit 2
          TAG="chart-$CHART-v$VERSION"
          sha=$(git -C consumer ls-remote origin "refs/tags/$TAG^{}" | awk 'NR == 1 {print $1}')
          if [[ ! "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            TAG="$CHART-v$VERSION"
            sha=$(git -C consumer ls-remote origin "refs/tags/$TAG^{}" | awk 'NR == 1 {print $1}')
          fi
          [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { echo "repair requires an existing annotated tag $TAG" >&2; exit 2; }
          echo "sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  repair:
    needs: resolve
    uses: 7K-Hiroba/workflows/.github/workflows/release-chart.yml@b26b53f5ba58a27d1973fec6dfa6469d0b93ba62 # v1.1.0
    with:
      root: .
      chart: "${{ inputs.chart }}"
      version: "${{ inputs.version }}"
      source-sha: "${{ needs.resolve.outputs.source-sha }}"
      repair: true
      standalone: true
    permissions: {contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, attestations: write, actions: read, artifact-metadata: write}

.github/workflows/compat-nightly.yml.content:
name: compatibility nightly
on:
  schedule: [{cron: "17 4 * * *"}]
  workflow_dispatch: {}
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  compat:
    uses: 7K-Hiroba/workflows/.github/workflows/compat-check.yml@b26b53f5ba58a27d1973fec6dfa6469d0b93ba62 # v1.1.0
    with: {root: ., mode: nightly}
    permissions: {contents: read, actions: read}
  notify:
    if: needs.compat.outputs.status == 'failure'
    needs: [compat]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read, issues: write}
    steps:
      - name: Open or update one early-warning issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
          RUN_URL: "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
        run: |
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --json number,title --jq '.[] | select(.title == "[compat] edge incompatibility") | .number' | head -n 1)
          if [[ -n "$number" ]]; then gh issue comment "$number" --body "Edge compatibility failed again: $RUN_URL"; else gh issue create --title '[compat] edge incompatibility' --body "Edge compatibility failed: $RUN_URL"; fi

AGENTS.md.content:
# Hiroba app agent guide

Use Conventional Commits and independently versioned components. Keep canonical observability in observability/ and regenerate chart/pack outputs with the workflow library. Keep releaseComponents synchronized with selected component paths; artifact-bound smoke inherits its target identity. All external actions and reusable workflows use full commit SHAs with version comments. Never add classic Helm indexes, UI Release assets, mutable release callers, or real-environment smoke execution. Use only public Inari SDK contracts.

CONTRIBUTING.md.content:
# Contributing

Open a pull request with Conventional Commits. All applicable workflow lanes must pass, including negative generated-output checks. Do not commit secrets, customer data, generated diagnostics, or registry credentials.

Read the [Hiroba governance](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md), [onboarding checklist](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/onboarding.md), and [trust-tier policy](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/trust-tiers.md). External contributions are currently paused while CLA coverage is reviewed; do not merge an external PR until the organization enables that process. Visit the [Hiroba organization profile](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba) for community context.

README.md.content:
# matrix-app

This is an experimental Hiroba community application repository generated by `inari hiroba init`. It uses the one-repository-per-application layout, independently versioned OCI artifacts, immutable workflow callers, and the public Inari SDK contracts.

## Before onboarding

Reserve the permanent app ID in [`7K-Hiroba/community`](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/registry/apps.json), create the owning maintainer team, and complete [application onboarding](https://github.com/7K-Hiroba/community/blob/main/docs/governance/onboarding.md). The generated sources do not claim that a repository, team, release, or trusted source already exists.

After the package is published and its trusted source is configured, deploy it with its canonical source-qualified identity:

~~~sh
inari deploy <source>/matrix-app --cluster <cluster-id> --file values.yaml
~~~

Short package names are local/display names only. Use the canonical `<source>/<package>` form when names collide.

## Development

Keep `package.yaml`/`template.yaml`, values schemas, canonical observability assets, generated chart/pack output, indexes, `releaseComponents`, and release metadata synchronized. Kind-qualified release identities prevent same-named components from colliding; artifact-bound smoke inherits its target identity. Run the repository's immutable PR callers and regeneration checks before submitting changes. Chartless observability still publishes the companion pack; chart-native output is optional. Fixture-only smoke suites are CI-only and are not application evidence.

The optional UI uses the stable `@7k-inari/ui-plugin-sdk@0.1.8` registry release and canonical `inari-ui-ext build`; no clone, postinstall, custom-webpack, or `@7k-hiroba` npm scope is used.

SECURITY.md.content:
# Security

Report vulnerabilities privately to the 7K-Hiroba security maintainers. This scaffold is CI-only and must never be deployed to production. Reviewed artifacts require valid cosign signatures, SLSA provenance, and current signed test evidence.

extension/Dockerfile.content:
FROM golang:1.26.3-bookworm@sha256:3bf5b04541eb4a37fe62aa1bc9c98a1dec09db9d2e79c1d2eb54e3c9d08dbca9 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/matrix-app ./cmd/matrix-app

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:816dc4d589459a7fe33b8a2e69edb70da56ffad7161f4b415937fa2bfe7e92e8
COPY --from=build /out/matrix-app /usr/local/bin/matrix-app
ENV SCAFFOLD_HTTP=true
EXPOSE 8080
USER 65532:65532
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/matrix-app"]

packages/matrix-app/README.md.content:
# app package

Platform-app fixture for the first-party OCI chart. Values are schema-validated and chart-native observability is disabled for companion-managed deployments.

packages/matrix-app/chart.yaml.content:
repoURL: oci://ghcr.io/7k-hiroba/matrix-app/charts
chart: matrix-app
namespace: matrix-app
channels:
  incubating: 0.1.0
  stable: 0.1.0

packages/matrix-app/package.yaml.content:
version: 0.1.0
channel: incubating
type: platform-app
description: First-party chart package used by the workflow scaffold
category: test

packages/matrix-app/tests/run.sh.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PACKAGE_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$PACKAGE_DIR/../.." && pwd)
CHART=${CHART_DIR:-$ROOT/charts/matrix-app}
RENDERED=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$RENDERED"' EXIT
helm template matrix-app "$CHART" --namespace matrix-app --values "$PACKAGE_DIR/values-defaults.yaml" > "$RENDERED"
grep -q 'kind: Deployment' "$RENDERED"
grep -q 'kind: Service' "$RENDERED"
grep -q 'runAsNonRoot: true' "$RENDERED"

packages/matrix-app/ui-hints.yaml.content:
fields:
  replicaCount:
    title: Replicas
    description: Number of synthetic extension replicas

packages/matrix-app/values-defaults.yaml.content:
replicaCount: 1
observability:
  enabled: false
  rules:
    enabled: false
